newsitem.title: USA: TRW posts record second-quarter results.
newsitem.headline: TRW posts record second-quarter results.

text.p: TRW Inc. Monday reported record second-quarter earnings, boosted by strong sales of car parts and revenues from space and defence contracts.

The company earned $134.4 million, or $1.05 a share on a fully-diluted basis, on $2.85 billion in revenues in the second quarter. In the year-ago period, it earned $130.5 million, or 98 cents a share, on revenues of $2.57 billion.
Analysts had expected TRW to report earnings of only $1.02 a share for the quarter.
TRW's stock hit a 52-week high at $61.31 on the news. It was up 44 cents at $60.75 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly before midday.

TRW said its space and defence business had profits of $82.2 million, up 29 percent from the 1996 second quarter. Sales grew 12 percent to $975.8 million as the Cleveland-based company carried out recent contracts.

Automotive profits for the quarter rose 7 percent to $180.9 million. Sales rose 10 percent to $1.88 billion due to acquisitions of European air bag and steering wheel operations, and greater demand for air bags, seat belts, and steering and engine parts, it said.
Automotive sales would have been even higher if not for a strong U.S. dollar and lower pricing in the North American air bag business, TRW said.
"Going forward, we will continue to supplement our organic growth with strategic acquisitions, outsourcing, and expansion in the emerging markets," said Chairman Joseph Gorman in a statement.
Gorman noted a number of ventures that will add to the company's future growth.
TRW opened a new plant in England to produce an environmentally friendly air bag inflator. It also expanded its electronics engineering centre in Michigan, adding seven engineering laboratories.

The company also started a joint venture with Toyoda Machine Works Ltd. to manufacture and sell power steering pumps to carmakers in Europe. It got a $59.2 million contract to develop and produce an engineering prototype of the digital processing system for the Department of Defence's next-generation Milsatcom satellite communications system.
TRW sold its flagship credit reporting company to Thomas Lee and Bain Capital for $1.1 billion in a deal that closed in September 1996.
